jsonNote: The code list and the map exactly as stored (codeList and map). Everything can also be done in the forms.

words.fromSource: the code of the line it is calculated from
words.lookup: a code looked up by {field} ({n, plural, one {# value} other {# values}}{hasDefault, select, yes {, otherwise {fallback}} other {}})

outcome.sourceCode: the code of its source line{has, select, yes { (now {code} {title})} other {}}
outcome.rulesForAny: {after, select, yes {Otherwise the} other {The}} rules for any line (above the table) decide, by the line's values.
outcome.noRule: {after, select, yes {Otherwise no} other {No}} rule gives these lines a code.

story.intro: {name} puts a code from its list of {n, plural, one {# code} other {# codes}}{hasLevels, select, yes { ({levels})} other {}} on every BoQ line, so the BoQ can be grouped and subtotalled by them. It never changes a quantity.
story.order: A line gets its code from the first of these that gives one:
story.stepDecision: your answer for the project, if a line was asked about (BoQ › Questions);
story.stepIfc: a code already on the elements in the IFC, when the model carries a classification named <settings>{names}</settings>;
story.stepMap:
this classification's rules: the table, one code per kind of BoQ line
{byCondition, plural, =0 {} one {, and # rule by condition} other {, and # rules by condition}}; when several apply, the higher priority wins{ask, select, yes { and a tie is asked about} other {}};
story.stepUnmapped: otherwise the line <settings>{mode, select, flag {stays without a code} ask {is asked about (it does not block the BoQ)} other {gets {code} {title}}}</settings>.
story.coverage: With the items of {ruleSet}: {sure} of {total} kinds of line always get a code, {some} only in some cases, {none} none.

table.hint: One row per BoQ item: every line that item makes gets the code picked here. Split a row when its lines need different codes, e.g. external and internal walls. Under a row: what else decides its code (rules by condition, which win when they have a higher priority).
table.itemsOfHint: Rule sets built on As modelled share its items, so one table serves all of them.
table.coded: {coded} of {total} rows coded in the table
table.acceptAll: Accept {n, plural, one {# suggestion} other {# suggestions}}
table.anyHint: These look at a line's values (material, element type…), not at which BoQ item made it, so they can apply to any row below that has no code of its own, or one with a lower priority. Highest priority first.
table.noRuleSets: No rule sets to take BoQ items from.
table.noPublished: This rule set has no published version yet: pick another one, or publish it first.
table.cannotResolve: This rule set cannot be resolved; check it in the Library.

groups.derived: Calculated from other items (formwork, paint, estimates…)

table.orphansTitle: Rows for lines this rule set does not have
table.orphansHint: Kept for other rule sets that do have them.
table.addValue: + own code for a {kind, select, material {material} other {element type}}…
table.uncoded: Nothing gives these lines a code

codes.hint: The codes lines can get, as a tree. {hasSep, select, yes {Parents follow from the separator “{sep}” (B.01 is under B).} other {Parents are set explicitly.}} In the BoQ, lines are grouped under these codes and their parents, with subtotals.
codes.empty: No codes yet. Add one, or import them from an Excel or CSV file.

about.title: About this list
about.name: Name
about.separatorHint: Gives each code its parent: with “.”, B.01 is under B.
about.idHint: The code list's id; the map of this classification points to it.
about.licenceHint: Official lists often may not be passed on. Company and client lists are your own data.
about.redistributable: may be shipped to other organisations

import.title: Import codes from a spreadsheet
import.hint: Excel (.xlsx) or CSV / TSV. Any layout: you will choose which column is the code, the title and the parent on the next step.
import.invalidFile: The file could not be read: {reason}
import.headerRowHint: The row with the column names; rows above it are skipped.
import.descriptionColumnHint: The code's written description (item text), if the file has one.

hierarchies.separator: from the codes (B.01 is under B)

import.previewRows: Rows {from}–{to} of {total}; the first one is the header.
import.stats: {codes, plural, one {# code} other {# codes}}, {top} at the top level, {levels, plural, one {# level} other {# levels}}.
import.merge: add to the existing codes (same code = update)
import.apply: Import {n, plural, =0 {codes} one {# code} other {# codes}}

rules.hint: Rules for what one code per BoQ item cannot say: lines of items with a tag, lines whose material or element type is something, hand-entered lines of a kind. When several rules give a line a code, the higher priority wins (table rows have 5, split rows 6); between equal priorities the one higher in this list wins{ask, select, yes {, or the line is asked about} other {}}.
rules.select: Select a rule, or add one.
rules.sectionTable: Written by the Codes per line table
rules.fromTable: Written by the Codes per line table; change it there.
rules.prioritySentence: Priority {priority}: {wins, select, yes {wins over the table's rows} other {the table's rows (priority 5 and 6) win over it}}{hasNote, select, yes {. {note}} other {.}}
rules.conditionHint: A condition can use the line's values: material, element type (dictionary terms, with “is a kind of”: UNDER(material, "concrete")), ifc_class, storey, storey_elevation, unit, tags, and keys. followed by what the line is split by, e.g. keys.type_name.

leaf.manualKind: Lines entered by hand, of kind

targetModes.lookup: looked up from a value of the line
targetModes.source: the code of the line it is calculated from

rules.fromSourceHint: Formwork, paint and other calculated lines take the code of the line they were calculated from.
rules.notInTable: When the value is not in the table
rules.priorityHint: Higher wins. Table rows have 5, split rows 6; give 7 or more to win over the table.

settings.order: A line's code comes from, in this order
settings.orderHint: The first that gives a code wins.

sources.decision: your answer for the project (when a line was asked about)
sources.map: this classification's rules (the table and the rules by condition)
sources.ifc: a code already on the elements in the IFC

settings.ifcNamesHint: An IfcClassification with one of these names counts as this list, e.g. Uniclass 2015.
settings.agreement: When a line's elements carry different codes

agreements.all: use it only if all agree

unmapped.ask: is asked about (does not block the BoQ)

settings.conflict: When rules of equal priority disagree

conflicts.first: the one higher in the list wins

settings.theMapHint: The map is the rules; the code list is the codes. They are saved together in this classification.
settings.name: Name
settings.extendsHint: Takes another map's rules; rules here replace them by id.
